summary: Let an authenticated tenant user securely connect an additional OIDC sign-in provider without relying on email-only account merging.
userImpact: Users can connect another configured OIDC provider from their profile and then use it for future sign-ins.
A login collision with an existing account returns an actionable conflict instead of a generic internal-server error.

changes: Adds authenticated endpoints that list and connect the current user's tenant-scoped OIDC providers.

notes: The existing external identity schema stores additional provider links; no migration is required.

security: A second provider is linked only after a current, non-revoked tenant session and a fresh provider authorization are both verified.
Signed state binds the link to the current user, tenant, provider, exact session ID and version, browser state cookie, PKCE verifier, and short expiry.
Pooled deployments continue to reject unauthenticated email-only account linking.
documentation: Documents the authenticated secondary-provider linking flow and its pooled-tenancy trust boundary.
knownLimitations: This change supports direct OIDC providers; SAML and LDAP account linking remain administrator-led.
rollback: Roll back the host release to remove the linking UI and endpoints; existing valid identity links remain usable and can be explicitly unlinked by an administrator.
validation: Focused OIDC route, signed-state, provisioning-service, frontend profile, OpenAPI, identity persistence, and host build checks.
Protected CI plus staging browser acceptance against the PostgreSQL SaaS environment are required before release.
